gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a passenger dispute with no impact never trips the G-sensor, so the clip stays in the normal loop folder, and that on the Vantrue N4 Pro S that folder holds only about 7 hours of three-camera driving on a 256 GB card (about 14 h on 512 GB, about 28 h on 1 TB) before the oldest clip is overwritten, unless the driver locks the clip with a short press of the power button behind the side cover.
standout_why: I compared three pages. productbible.com (cited) only says 'Three cameras fill a card fast' and recommends at least 256 GB. It gives no hours and does not explain why a dispute does not lock its clip. dashlore.com (cited) gives card maximums and says an SSD gives 'days of three-channel footage' but gives no figure. redlinecargarage.com (cited) gives no hours and only says the camera overwrites the oldest clips when the card is full. None of the three explains that a G-sensor lock needs an impact, gives a loop-folder share or hours per card, or says where the manual lock button is. ChatGPT's answer suggested 256–512 GB without saying that 256 GB does not cover one long shift.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue N4 Pro S as the pick and changes what goes with it. A full-time driver needs a 1 TB card, which the N4 Pro S supports according to Vantrue's store, so that one full shift is still on the card the next day. The driver also has to lock any ride that may turn into a complaint by hand: a short press of the power button, or the remote sold in Vantrue's bundle. On a 256 GB card a 10-hour shift overwrites its own first 3 hours. This favours cameras that take 1 TB cards (the N4 Pro S, N4S and N5S according to Vantrue's store) over 512 GB models. It also means the page should tell rideshare drivers to lock clips manually and size the card to the shift, rather than only quoting resolution.

findings.label: What locks a clip automatically
findings.value: Only a jolt big enough for the G-sensor: 'When the car get hit, the camera senses the vibration, the video will be locked into the "event" folder.' Otherwise 'The vibration is not big enough and the video goes to the "normal folder".'
findings.note: Vantrue's own words; no model named. A verbal or behaviour dispute in the back seat causes no impact, so its clip goes to the normal (overwritable) folder.

findings.label: Event folder cap
findings.value: 'When the total event folder takes up 30% of the whole memory card, the event videos will recycle themselves. The old event videos will be erased.'
findings.note: The same FAQ also says event files 'can not be overwritten, but need you delete them manually'. The page contradicts itself, so locked clips should still be copied off the card.

findings.label: Loop recording off
findings.value: 'The dash cam will stop recording when the card is full if you turn off the loop recording.'
findings.note: So loop recording has to stay on, and overwriting is how the camera works, not a fault.

findings.label: Measured file size per minute, all three cameras
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk, EricSan, post #1, 2025-07-20)
findings.note: EricSan printed the cabin bitrate as 0.98 Mb/s. 74,410 KB/min works out to about 9.9 Mb/s, so the printed figure is a typo; I used the file sizes. The rear is printed as '2592x1440P'. Firmware is not stated.

findings.label: Hours of three-camera driving kept before overwrite (loop share of the card)
findings.value: About 7 h on 256 GB, about 14 h on 512 GB, about 28 h on 1 TB
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk, EricSan)
findings.note: My arithmetic: 417,790 KB/min × 60 = 25.1 GB/h (KB taken as 1,000 bytes; 25.7 GB/h if KiB). Loop share is 70% of the card (from the Dash Cam Guys guide, row below): 256 × 0.7 = 179.2 GB ÷ 25.1 = 7.1 h; 512 → 358.4 GB → 14.3 h; 1,000 → 700 GB → 27.9 h. A card's usable space is a little below its label, so these are upper bounds.

findings.label: Loop/event split and hours per card (retailer's own calculation)
findings.value: 'Normal loop recording gets 70 per cent of the card'; loop 'overwrites within its own 70 per cent and cannot borrow from the event area'; 3-channel hours: 64 GB 1 h 45 m, 128 GB 3 h 30 m, 256 GB 7 h, 512 GB 13 h 50 m
findings.source_title: Vantrue SD Card Sizes and Real Recording Times (Dash Cam Guys)
findings.note: Based on a 57.5 Mb/s total from DashCamTalk measurements of August 2025 × 0.7. The page says the 70% split is in the N4 Pro, N4 Pro S and S1 Pro Max manuals but not in the N5 manual. It agrees with my figures to within about 0.5 h.

findings.label: Manual lock control
findings.value: Short press of the power button locks the current video; long press is power. The button sits behind a hidden panel that also covers the microSD slot and reset button
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk, EricSan)
findings.note: EricSan: 'power button (long press) which doubles with with Lock Video button (short press)'; the cover 'covers the SD card slot, the Power/Lock Video button and the Reset button'. Opening a cover mid-ride is awkward, which is why the remote in Vantrue's bundle matters (next row).

findings.label: Max card and lock-remote bundle on Vantrue's US store
findings.value: Up to 1 TB microSD; bundle with VP03 hardwire kit, 256 GB card, CPL filter and remote: $428.99 (list $644.95), in stock
findings.source_title: Bundle: N4 Pro S + VP03 Hardwire Kit + 256GB Card + CPL + Remote Controller | Vantrue
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search on vantrue.com on 2026-11-21. The camera alone shows $279.99 (list $469.99), and the feature list says 'Up to 1TB microSD Support'. The bundle's 256 GB card holds about 7 h of 3-channel driving (rows above). The product page itself returned HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and storecheck product.

findings.label: Manual lock control and cabin IR
findings.value: Same short-press-power lock button; cabin IR LEDs switch on automatically when the menu setting is 'Auto' and 'are NOT visible with the naked eye while they are illuminated'
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue Nexus 5S (DashCamTalk, EricSan, posts #2–#3, Sep 2025)
findings.note: TonyM (post #13) gives about 9.8 Mb/s for the two 1080p cabin cameras, but the full four-camera bitrate table is an image, so I computed no hours for the N5S.

findings.label: Max card on Vantrue's US store
findings.value: Up to 1 TB microSD; $199.99 (list $359.99), in stock
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search on 2026-11-21: 'support for up to 1TB microSD cards'; 2.7K front plus 2.5K cabin and rear.

findings.label: Uber's own handling of driver dashcam footage
findings.value: US drivers can register their own dashcam in the Driver app (Account → App settings → Video recording → Dashcam registration) 'and provide evidence for accident claims'; Uber's in-app recordings are 'deleted after 14 days' unless a safety report or insurance claim is filed
findings.source_title: Recording for added peace of mind | Uber
findings.note: Uber's in-app recordings are kept for 14 days, while the dash cam's own loop on a 256 GB N4 Pro S keeps about 7 hours. Footage the driver wants to submit has to be locked or copied off the card.
